domainLookupsHint: Checks contacts' domain proofs. The resolver sees which domain.
domainLookupsInfo: When a contact shares a domain proof, this app looks up its record through {{name}}, a DNS-over-HTTPS resolver. If it cannot be reached, the next of Quad9, Cloudflare and Google is asked. The resolver learns which domain was looked up and when, never your chats. Proofs published as a file on a website are downloaded from that website, which sees your IP address.
hyperdhtHint: Optional fallback when WebRTC fails. Empty: WebRTC only.
hyperdhtInfo: Lets chats use HyperDHT from this browser. The relay forwards encrypted bytes: it sees your address and when you talk, never what you say.
irohHint: Used when WebRTC cannot connect. One per line, up to four.
irohInfo: A browser cannot send the UDP packets Iroh uses, so Iroh chats here go through a relay. It sees which devices talk and when, never what they say: the connection is encrypted end to end.
readRelaysHint: Finds a first contact sooner. Relays see which keys it looks up.
readRelaysInfo: This app reads the Mainline DHT directly. With this on, it also reads through the Pkarr relays below.
relaysHint: One per line. They only see signed, encrypted packets.
relaysInfoDirect: Contacts on the web and in the extension cannot reach the Mainline DHT and read through relays, so this app writes to them too.
relaysInfoWeb: Browsers cannot reach the Mainline DHT directly, so relays do it for them. They never carry your messages, calls or services. Every relay listed is used.
title: Network
turnHint: Optional. Used only when a direct connection fails.
turnInfo: It forwards encrypted WebRTC packets. It is connectivity infrastructure, not a Ghostly server.
